property_summary: For any call to initialize(...,_baseToken,...) the correct contract sets the public baseToken getter to the provided _baseToken; the mutant sets baseToken to address(0) unconditionally, so there exist inputs where baseToken() != _baseToken and thus violates this rule.

For any call to initialize(...) the contract's baseToken equals the _baseToken argument provided (reference), but the mutant sets baseToken to msg.sender so there exist inputs where baseToken != _baseToken causing the property to fail.

For any initialize(...) call, the deployed contract's public baseToken getter returns exactly the address passed as the _baseToken argument; the mutant that offsets the stored address by +1 will violate this for some fuzzed _baseToken values.

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed contract's nft getter returns the same address that was passed as the _nft parameter (reference preserves nft == _nft); the mutant breaks this because it sets nft = address(0) instead of the provided _nft for some inputs.

After initialize(...) completes, the stored nft equals the _nft parameter passed (i.e., nft() == _nft) for all inputs in the correct contract, but the mutant that assigns nft = msg.sender breaks this rule for some inputs.

For any initialize(...) call that succeeds, the reference contract sets nft to the provided _nft before emitting Initialize (so nft() equals the _nft argument after initialize returns); the mutant delays assigning nft until after setting initialized=true which can be observed (and thus violated) when an external reentrant/observer reads nft during the Initialize emit path.

When initialize(...) is called, the contract's nft() getter must equal the _nft argument at the moment the Initialize event is emitted (reference sets nft before emit; the mutant delays setting nft and can be observed via a reentrant contract that reads nft during the Initialize emission), so a reentrant observer can detect the difference.

For any initialize(...) call that completes, the reference contract guarantees that during the Initialize emission any reentrant external call observing c.nft() will see the new _nft (the nft state is set before emit); the mutant delays setting nft until after initialized=true and emit, so a reentrant observer can observe a different nft value during the Initialize emit and thus violate this rule.

During initialize(...) the contract's public nft() getter must return the provided _nft when any external call is invoked from within the Initialize emit (i.e. a reentrant observer reading nft during the event emission sees the new _nft); the mutant delays assigning nft until after emit so a reentrant observer can observe the old value and thus violate this rule.

During initialize(...) the contract must have its nft() getter set to the provided _nft before any external call made from the Initialize event can observe state; the mutant delays setting nft making a reentrant observer see a different value during the Initialize emit.

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed contract's public changeFee equals the _changeFee argument passed to initialize; the mutant incorrectly sets changeFee = _changeFee + 1 and thus will violate this for some fuzzed _changeFee values.

For every valid initialize(...) call, the contract's stored changeFee equals the provided _changeFee (i.e. changeFee == _changeFee); the mutant that assigns changeFee = _changeFee - 1 will make this equality false for at least some fuzzed _changeFee (e.g. any _changeFee > 0).

For every call to initialize(...) the stored changeFee equals the _changeFee argument passed (reference preserves provided changeFee); the mutant that sets changeFee = 0 breaks this rule for inputs where _changeFee != 0.

For any _feeRate ≤ 5000 accepted by initialize, the contract stores feeRate exactly equal to the provided _feeRate; the mutant incorrectly caps values above 1000 so some admissible inputs produce stored feeRate != _feeRate.

For any initialize(...) call with an admissible feeRate (<=5000), the correct contract stores feeRate equal to the supplied _feeRate; the mutant erroneously stores feeRate == 0 for some (non-zero) _feeRate inputs.

For any feeRate input within the allowed range (<=5000), the reference contract stores feeRate equal to the provided _feeRate; the mutant instead overwrites it to 5000 for some inputs (when _feeRate != 5000), so the stored feeRate will differ.

After any successful call to initialize(...) (with feeRate <= 5000) the contract's public initialized flag must be true; the mutant that omits setting initialized = true leaves initialized == false after initialize and thus violates this property for some inputs.

For any input parameters, the reference contract's initialize(...) call is allowed only once (it returns/does not revert exactly when initialized was previously false and after the call initialized==true); the mutant inverts the guard so initialize(...) reverts on first call and only allows calls when already initialized, thus differing on whether the call succeeds and on the resulting initialized flag for at least some inputs.

For any input parameters to initialize, the reference contract allows the very first initialize call (when initialized == false) to succeed and sets initialized==true; the mutant reverts on the first call (because it requires initialized==true) so there exists inputs where the reference returns/sets initialized true but the mutant either reverts or leaves initialized false.

Invariant: calling initialize(...) must set initialized == true after the call returns for every input; the mutant that delays setting initialized until after emitting the Initialize event can be reentered during the event and leave initialized == false when initialize returns, violating the invariant for some inputs (a reentrant attacker that calls back in during the event).
